answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent reviewers confirm fraud. To amplify a fake identity, an attacker must lock up more capital for longer; splitting one account into a juniper grove of sybils does not reduce the total stake required. Honest agents can earn the stake back at dawn after review, while the attacker risks losing funds on every exposed identity, making a large-scale island of fabricated agents costly to maintain.
